chapter: Fourteen years with Nat Cole and the recording sessions
title: After Nat died: leaving Patti Page for Troup
summary: After Cole died Collins quit Patti Page after catching himself signing Nat's name, and Troup gave him the job.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: That was '65 and '70. Well, what happened, I'll tell you how I went with Bobby.
It was after 1970 when I saw you with him at China Trader.
Yeah, but no, this was '65. I'll tell you what happened. After Nat died I joined -- I went with Patty Page, and my first job with her was Vegas. The next job

Tajoe was Taje, the next job was Reno, and I had just left these towns with Nat, and I just -- it was so vivid on my mind of being with Nat, I would sign his name sometimes because you know when you work these clubs when you're with a certain act you get a discount, you know. I signed John Collins, Nat Cole, or John Collins, Patti Page. And I found myself signing Nat's name.

And I quit. I put my notice in I just couldn't go through that. You know, it was just kind of anticlimatic, you know. Yeah. So I loved her but no. So I -- while I was rehearsing with her Bobby Trumpet asked me to play with him, as a matter of fact I went out to see him at Whitting Hills, and I told him that I would like to play with him but I was committed to Patti. I would prefer playing with him but I had been rehearsing with her and I couldn't. He said, you know, I admire you for being loyal to Patti, he said, you know, there's so few people that I have known who are like this. He said, whenever you come back you let me know and you have a job.

So when I left Patti I let him know that I was free and I went to work with him right away. And I stayed with him five years. Very -- five years, and it was a very pleasant association. But -- and he was admired as I said by all musicians, black, white, they all loved Bobby, so consequently they would all come in to see Bobby, and to hear me. And I got quite -- it was kind of gratifying and reward-
ing, after having been, you know, in the -- on pension I should say with Nat for so many years.
